thread:
sam: Heads-up — p99 for /v1/chat in eu-central spiked ~320ms after we shifted 10% traffic to the new route policy. p50/p95 unchanged. anyone seen a similar tail-only jump? :thinking:
nina: I noticed that too. Splitting dashboard by endpoint shows /v1/chat/stream has the biggest delta. transport_time is the outlier at the tail.
oliver: two quick checks: (1) are we including client-side retries in the rollup? (2) which percentile source are we using (tdigest vs sample-rollup)? mixing can surprise p99.
sam: good call. dashboard uses 'percentile_source=auto' for the rollout view. i'll force `percentile_source=tdigest` and re-eval.
metrics-bot: NOTE: rollup-config mismatch detected for route '/v1/chat' — ingest tags vary across canary hosts (transport_ms tag present on 3/8 hosts).
nina: if some hosts export transport separately, then rollups that sum transport+server may double-count when merging tdigest-derived percentiles. canary tagging looks inconsistent.
oliver: also check transport-level tags for proxy vs gateway — sometimes gateway adds its own transport_ms, then the router adds another. run `esql "select tags from metrics where route='/v1/chat' limit 20"` to eyeball.
sam: ran a quick query, confirmed inconsistent tags across canary nodes. interestingly, p95 on nodes that have the tag is fine — the p99 is influenced by a few samples from nodes that also show elevated TCP syn->estab times.
ops-bot: ALERT: NIC errors annotated on canary hosts host-12, host-14 between 10:22-10:28 UTC — see ops ticket #INC-4821.
nina: that aligns with the client-ip_subnet slice I did — tail concentrated on a handful of subnets (likely affected by NIC flaps).
oliver: conclusion hypothesis: tail jump driven by network-level transient on some canary hosts + inconsistent exporter tagging causing aggregation oddities. fix path: (A) roll back routing weight if customer-facing SLOs impacted; (B) normalize exporter tags and re-ingest samples; (C) re-run pctl after cleaning retries and forcing tdigest.
sam: agree. for now i'll roll canary back to 0% and open a bug on tag normalization. leaving ticket for infra to check NICs.
nina: can we also add a console UX note: show percentile_source next to pctl selector and a hover explainer about tag-sensitivity? even a small hint would reduce confusion.
ops-bot: ops ticket created: INC-4821. assigned to infra-net.
oliver: small test to reproduce locally: run the in-memory exporter with/without transport_ms tag and feed two tdigest streams, see how merged p99 behaves. sharing a snippet:
```
# pseudo
exporter_a: tags: transport_ms
exporter_b: tags: none
merge_streams(a,b) -> p99 drift
```

sam: thanks — i'll coordinate rollback and file the exporter normalization bug. will update thread after infra confirms NIC status. :thumbsup:
